claims.text: Replacing TOR-TILD's EAM reference with an ML-IAP trained on high-temperature liquid configurations will improve reference-target phase-space overlap.
Replacing the EAM reference with the liquid-trained ML-IAP will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch.
Al-Cr-Co-Fe-Ni is a multicomponent high-entropy alloy system relevant to high-temperature atomistic calculations.
The proposed method applies to CrCoFeMnNi and AlCrCoFeNi in both solid and liquid states near melting.
An ab initio training set enriched with high-temperature liquid configurations can capture a wide range of liquid atomic arrangements.
A temperature window of approximately 50 K below to 50 K above melting is applicable for testing the intervention.
Sampling within approximately ±50 K of melting will cover both solid and liquid regimes.
Configurational diversity in these HEAs is especially pronounced in the high-temperature liquid regime.
A flexible ML architecture can learn the relevant many-body interactions from ab initio data.
An optimized interaction cutoff will capture medium-range order.
Traditional EAM potentials miss complex many-body interactions and diverse configurations in the ab initio liquid.
Including ab initio liquid configurations in training will improve the ML-IAP's representation of liquid configurations.
Improved representation of liquid configurations will enhance phase-space overlap between the reference and ab initio target.
Enhanced phase-space overlap will reduce mismatch along the integrated free-energy path.
The ML-IAP free-energy result will approach direct ab initio calculations to within ±5 meV/atom.
TOR-TILD's EAM references have significant difficulty representing diverse ab initio liquid configurations.
TOR-TILD's EAM references produce noticeable thermodynamic-integration path mismatches.
ML-IAP performance may degrade for compositions and temperatures substantially outside the training domain.
